cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code creates a markdown parser with configurable HTML rendering. When html:true, user input could potentially bypass neutralization and render as raw HTML, enabling XSS.

connection.evidence: User post content flows through markdownify() -> parser.render(raw). Admin-configurable settings control parser behavior via _self.config passed to Remarkable constructor.

diff_causality.evidence: The parser initialization with configurable options enables the HTML rendering capability. Reverting would remove the configurable parser but not necessarily the vulnerability mechanism.

security_control.evidence: Default configuration has html:false, but admin can enable it. No evidence of input sanitization or HTML escaping in the markdownify path.
security_control.required_control: HTML input sanitization/escaping when HTML rendering is enabled
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-79 requires neutralization of user input when rendered as HTML to prevent script injection
security_control.deficiency_evidence: When html:true is configured, user input passes directly to HTML rendering without demonstrated neutralization controls

concrete_impact.evidence: XSS impact is plausible but depends on downstream usage and whether html:true is actually configured and used with untrusted input.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the parser would not be initialized with configurable options, potentially preventing HTML rendering capability but breaking markdown functionality entirely.
supporting_evidence: Parser initialized with user-configurable _self.config including 'html' option
markdownify function passes raw user input directly to parser.render()
Admin interface allows configuration changes including enabling HTML rendering
contradicting_evidence: Default configuration has html:false, providing safe default
No evidence that html:true is actually configured or used in vulnerable context
unresolved_facts: Whether admin interface properly validates/sanitizes HTML configuration changes
Whether Remarkable library provides any built-in XSS protection when html:true
Whether other input sanitization occurs before markdown processing
Whether html:true configuration is actually deployed in production
review_comment: The parser initialization allows HTML rendering to be enabled via admin configuration. When html:true is set, user post content could render as raw HTML without demonstrated neutralization. Ensure HTML rendering is either disabled or that proper input sanitization is implemented when enabled. Consider maintaining html:false as the only safe configuration or implementing strict content security policies.
